Authorized questions

Identity and permission must become an enforced query boundary.

How it works

Try one example

Casey sells for Harbor. A rep may see their own sales. A manager may see the team. These are illustrative access rules, simulated locally in this browser.

Rules and supporting detail

Identity becomes a query boundary

Signed-in identity
→
Resolved person
→
Allowed scope
→
Scoped query

Authentication establishes who signed in. Identity matching links that account to a business person. Authorization determines which records they may access. Each step needs its own evidence.

A model can help interpret a question, but a trusted service must enforce the permitted filters. The public demo illustrates the decision; it is not a production security implementation.

A clear answer when data is unavailable

Permission to query is not proof that a query succeeded. If the data service is unavailable, return that state instead of inventing a number. If “we” could mean several teams or periods, ask for the missing scope before running a query.

StateAppropriate response
Outside permitted teamDeny the requested scope
Ambiguous questionClarify the missing meaning
Permitted, service unavailableExplain that no current result was retrieved
